catalog.title: Measure-only preserving Markov transports characterize mass-stationarity

metadata.title: Measure-only preserving Markov transports characterize mass-stationarity
metadata.description:
This research note gives an affirmative answer to Last and Thorisson's formal Problem 7.3 (Annals of Probability, 2009). On any locally compact second countable Hausdorff Abelian group, for an arbitrary jointly measurable ambient flow, a sigma-finite measure Q and a nonzero covariant locally finite Radon random measure xi, full ambient invariance under every invariant xi-preserving xi-measurable Markov transport is equivalent to joint mass-stationarity. The proof derives the joint Mecke identity using oriented local symmetric transports away from measure periods and normalized period-subgroup transports. It requires neither a standard Borel ambient space, a sigma-finite marginal law of xi nor finite intensity. The classical Mecke/Palm and Palm/mass-stationarity equivalences and converse transport invariance are credited. The narrower non-discrete deterministic Cox-allocation converse is not claimed.

Two independent extensive bounded priority reviews and a fresh adjudication identified no exact earlier resolution in the sources inspected. This is not an exhaustive literature certificate, worldwide-firstness guarantee or certification of present openness. Unread final editions, including the final 2015 SPA body, and identified audiovisual and citation-coverage gaps are disclosed in the supporting priority note. Statements cited from author editions are not asserted identical to unread final versions.

The verification archive contains the standalone manuscript source, claim and credit records, priority qualifications, unchanged original author and independent finite exact control programs, complete expected outputs and a portable hash-and-output verifier. The finite controls cover examples of preservation, reversal gates, period kernels and hidden ambient states. Legacy background-Cox controls do not certify the stricter intensity-erased Cox-allocation question. Finite computation supplements the analytic proof and proves neither the general theorem nor novelty. catalog.title: Exact chordal separation of spherical Fibonacci points

metadata.title: Exact chordal separation of spherical Fibonacci points
metadata.description:
This research note proves the exact finite separation conjecture stated in Johann S. Brauchart's OWR 40/2012 contribution, published in 2013. For every integer n at least 3, the rational unshifted unit-sphere configuration with Fn points has minimum Euclidean chord 2/sqrt(Fn), uniquely at the north pole and its first latitude point. A latitude-longitude inequality reduces the all-pair lower bound to classical Fibonacci dual-lattice arithmetic. An elementary unimodular-basis proof of the weaker arithmetic bound needed here makes the argument self-contained. The older construction, pole upper bound and Zaremba product index are credited. The theorem does not assert optimal sphere packing or apply to midpoint, irrational-angle or arbitrary-cardinality variants.

catalog.title: An explicit SU(5) lens-space counterexample to the printed Guadagnini-Pilo conjecture

metadata.title: An explicit SU(5) lens-space counterexample to the printed Guadagnini-Pilo conjecture
metadata.description:
For the ordinary full SU(5) Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant at WZW level 5, shifted level 10, L(5,1) and L(5,2) have fundamental group Z/5 but unequal nonzero magnitudes. With S3 normalization equal to one, their squared magnitudes are 3475 + 1550 sqrt(5) and 4025 + 1800 sqrt(5). An exact A4 root-lattice reduction and reproducible cyclotomic certificates establish this counterexample to Conjecture 7.5 as printed on p.474 of Ohtsuki's collection (volume nominally 2002, published 1 June 2004), conditional on established full modular-category and RT/Hansen-Takata surgery inputs.

Historical priority remains unresolved. Takahito Kuriya's directly relevant preprint, The LMO invariant and the Guadagnini-Pilo conjecture for lens spaces, could not be obtained. We cannot establish that it does not already contain or circumscribe this result. No first counterexample, exhaustive novelty clearance, current global open status or new historical resolution is claimed. Bounded source comparisons and their limitations are documented.

catalog.title: The mixed point spectrum of a matrix contraction on its closed unit ball

metadata.title: The mixed point spectrum of a matrix contraction on its closed unit ball
metadata.description:
We explicitly answer the mixed point-spectrum converse left open after Theorem 3.1.14(i) of Kari Valentina Kuster's 2015 thesis and stated only as an inclusion in her 2016 Pure Koopmanism contribution. For a matrix contraction on a finite-dimensional complex space with any complex norm, acting by composition on all continuous complex functions on its closed unit ball, every unimodular eigenfunction factors through the contractive peripheral spectral projection. The unimodular point spectrum is exactly the multiplicative group generated by the peripheral matrix eigenvalues. An elementary self-contained proof yields the full point and Banach-operator spectrum classification, including singular, nilpotent and nonnormal cases.

The missing exclusion is a short specialization of classical Jacobs-de Leeuw-Glicksberg theory and the prior all-peripheral calculation. The open-disk eigenvalues, prior peripheral and nilpotent cases, and the already immediate full-disk consequence are explicitly credited. A bounded primary-source audit found no earlier explicit completion in the examined scope; source-edition and coverage gaps are documented. No worldwide firstness, exhaustive literature absence, continuous 2015-2026 openness, new general decomposition theorem, or novel full-disk spectrum is claimed.

catalog.title: Consistent spectral recovery of smooth reversible diffusion tensors at a fixed lag

metadata.title: Consistent spectral recovery of smooth reversible diffusion tensors at a fixed lag
metadata.description:
This research note proves almost-sure consistency of a specified finite-rank empirical spectral-equation estimator for a general smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic tensor and unknown positive smooth invariant density. The domain is known, bounded, connected and smooth, in dimension at least two. Observations are exact stationary positions at one known fixed positive lag, reflection is conormal, and fixed pointwise ellipticity and density bounds are known. The tensor and its separately fitted divergence converge locally uniformly; an ellipticity-clipped tensor converges globally in L2. The covariance is 2S/mu and the interior drift is (div S)/mu. The proof supplies boundary-corrected dependent-data kernel estimates, full spectral-jet excitation, continuous functional calculus through empirical spectral collisions and eigenvector-free measurability.

This supplies a convergence analysis for the smooth setting of the spectral reconstruction question posed by Reiss with Chorowski, Gobet and Hoffmann in OWR24/2017, published in 2018. Earlier general nonparametric spectral residual fitting and transition-eigenvalue power weighting by Crommelin and Vanden-Eijnden, reversible identification, scalar fixed-lag inference, cutoff spectral excitation, deterministic tensor reconstruction and classical elliptic regularity are credited. A bounded dated primary-source audit located no encompassing theorem, with explicit edition/access gaps including the uninspected Crommelin-Vanden-Eijnden 2011 publisher-final body; no worldwide firstness guarantee is made. The supplementary classical regularization application is a new derivation of another estimator during this audit, not an earlier published resolution or a proof of the spectral objective. No rate, minimax, computational-efficiency, rough/nonreversible model, added sensor-noise or general-domain numerical implementation claim is made.

The verification archive contains the standalone source, supplementary derivations, eight unchanged finite-control programs, selected expected scientific outputs, an actual-process replay runner, provenance and source-edition limits. catalog.title: A complete negatively curved observation Gramian with two-state ambiguity

metadata.title: A complete negatively curved observation Gramian with two-state ambiguity
metadata.description:
We give a nonvacuous two-dimensional counterexample to the manifold conjecture printed by Krener in OWR11/2009. A smooth observed system on a connected closed genus-three surface has zero dynamics and output in R17 obtained by composing a connected two-sheeted hyperbolic covering with a smooth Nash isometric embedding. Its exact finite-time differential observation Gramian is P_T=T*pi^*g. For every fixed positive T it is geodesically complete with actual sectional curvature -1/T and uniform positive upper and lower bounds relative to any fixed smooth background metric and a fixed finite normalized atlas. The history map is locally injective but every attained history has exactly two initial states.

The construction is an application of classical constructions, with Nash, covering classification, hyperbolic geometry and older local/global observability ambiguity explicitly credited. A bounded primary-source audit, including complete readings of Dirr2009 and Kang2013 and a fresh independent adversarial priority assessment, found no verified earlier explicit complete construction in inspected sources. Those two named access gaps are closed; older uninspected originals and corpus limits are documented. No absolute firstness, continuous seventeen-year openness, new covering/Nash mechanism, or first refutation of every literal dimensional reading is claimed. A strengthened question restricted to one global Euclidean state domain is outside this result.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting, reproducing and adversarially reviewing the work. This is an unrefereed preprint without conventional human peer review. catalog.title: Focal pedal area ratios of closed elliptic billiards

metadata.title: Focal pedal area ratios of closed elliptic billiards
metadata.description:
This research note proves the focal pedal area equality observed by Reznik, Garcia and Koiller in April 2020 for every primitive closed elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate elliptical caustic, including coprime star orbits. More precisely, the signed supporting-line pedal areas of the outer tangent polygon and the original chord polygon are proportional by a positive phase-independent constant common to both foci. A common pair of simple poles, local original and adjacent outer cancellations, strict real signed positivity, and compact-torus residue matching yield the proof. Reversal and positive integral repetitions are covered explicitly.

An exact triangular certificate disproves the interpretation that the common focal ratio itself is constant over the family. Prior observation of the equality, its known primitive-even symmetry proof, an explicit triangular consequence of old geometric theorems, the classical nonconstancy corollary, canonical coordinates and established Jacobi principal-part methods are credited. The specialized local arguments already appeared in companion repository work and are reconstructed here. A bounded primary-source priority audit identified no earlier proof across the full stated domain; no absolute firstness, independently new invariant, triangular novelty, new negative theorem, or new general method is claimed. Hyperbolic or collapsed caustics, diameter walks, unsigned lobe areas and segment-clamped projections are excluded.

The supporting archive contains the editable standalone source, the conditional triangular deduction, exact and finite high-precision verification programs, actual outputs, provenance and source/edition limitations. Numerical diagnostics are not interval-certified and do not replace the universal proof. This is an unrefereed preprint. catalog.title: Asymptotic LOCC dense coding with the symmetric four-qubit W state

metadata.title: Asymptotic LOCC dense coding with the symmetric four-qubit W state
metadata.description:
We answer the historical distributed dense-coding question for the symmetric four-qubit W state in the local-unitary model of Bruss and collaborators. Two independent senders transmit one qubit each to different receivers. A complete Bell instrument at one receiver retains a classical-quantum output at the other; the established cq multiple-access coding theorem gives an achievable sum-rate supremum at least 3/2 + h2(1/4) = 2.311278124459... bits per resource copy. Both senders can achieve 9/8 bits per copy with vanishing uniform average error, establishing the original-model LOCC-DC classification.

The Bell decomposition, Bell forwarding, cqMAC coding theorem and prior general MAC dense-coding framework are explicitly credited. The bounded primary-literature audit found no earlier explicit or established-equivalent achievement of the exact target in inspected sources; specific access and version limitations are documented. No categorical firstness or worldwide continued openness, exact optimal capacity, one-copy advantage, zero-error or maximal-error claim is made.

catalog.title: Closedness and attractive approximation of binary MTP2 edge models

metadata.title: Closedness and attractive approximation of binary MTP2 edge models
metadata.description:
For every fixed finite simple graph, this research note proves that the binary MTP2 probability distributions admitting finite nonnegative unary and original-edge factors are exactly the pointwise limits of strictly positive attractive Ising distributions on the same graph. It consequently answers Conjecture 1 in Lauritzen's 2022 Oberwolfach problem statement affirmatively, including zero probabilities and the source's literal edge-only conventions for isolated vertices and empty graphs. The proof explicitly handles pins, deterministic equalities and implication supports, aggregates interactions across equality classes, constructs positive attractive approximations, and uses a classical residual-flow representation to bound finite factors with a nonvanishing normalizer.

The note credits the toric support framework of Geiger, Meek and Sturmfels, the MTP2 graphical results of Lauritzen, Uhler and Zwiernik and Fallat et al., the natural-support factorization framework of Kahle and Sullivant, and classical graph-cut and residual-flow tools. The supplement gives the additional facial-lattice support derivation underlying the comparison. The accompanying negative answers to the separate factorization conjectures are credited to the exact earlier counterexample of Gandolfi and Lenarda, published April 13, 2017. No new-counterexample, first-discovery or exhaustive historical-priority claim is made. Portable exact verification code and generated results accompany the proofs; bounded finite checks do not replace the arbitrary-graph proof.

This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively in developing the arguments, searching primary literature, writing, coding, reproduction and independent adversarial review. Automated reviews and exact computations are not external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification; neither is claimed.

catalog.title: Full 5-torsion of the regular-pentagon quintic pencil

metadata.title: Full 5-torsion of the regular-pentagon quintic pencil
metadata.description:
This research note computes all twenty-five geometric fifth-torsion points of the genus-one normalization of the regular-pentagon quintic pencil in McCallum's Question 17 in the AIM workshop problem list on rational and integral points. For an explicit equation normalization over K=Q(sqrt(5)), it gives a cubic model, both birational maps, a degree-ten residual polynomial and both ordinate branches. The complete division field is K(sqrt(5+2sqrt(5)),zeta_5,theta), where theta^5=lambda+phi^5 and phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. Its degree is four or twenty, with the exact splitting criterion and Galois action specified. The computation covers every elliptic normalization, including the allowed cuspidal plane member.

The proof applies classical Tate normal form, Fisher's full-level modular cover, Verdure's full-torsion specialization criterion, Morton's prior explicit Tate torsion formulas and residual polynomial, division-polynomial theory and the Weil pairing. It credits the source's known infinity subgroup and the earlier partial computation. No first-discovery or first-priority claim is made. The verification supplement supplies portable exact symbolic and standard-library arithmetic controls, independent finite group-law checks, deliberate mutants, primary references and a bounded priority audit. Nonregular or star-polygon variants and Tate-Shafarevich or local-solubility constructions are outside the stated theorem.

This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively in derivation, computation, literature research, writing, reproduction and adversarial review. Automated reviews are not independent external human peer review; no such human review or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.

catalog.title: A counterexample to Takao's self-duality question

metadata.title: A counterexample to Takao's self-duality question
metadata.description:
For every prime p greater than 3 and every n at least 3, this research note constructs a finite flat commutative group scheme over W(closure of F_p), killed by p and of rank p^(2n), with quasi-supersingular special fiber, such that both the special fiber and its Witt-ring lift fail Cartier self-duality. It gives an explicit negative answer to the higher-rank question following Proposition 2 on page 2479 of Naotake Takao's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 42/2023.

The proof uses an explicit six-dimensional Dieudonne module, a supersingular elliptic p-torsion filtration, an image-intersection invariant and a finite Honda complement. These are applications of established Dieudonne and finite Honda theory, with the classical cyclic-word framework credited. No first-discovery or first-priority claim is made. The verification supplement includes portable standard-library controls, source references, the bounded priority audit and its access/version limitations.

This is an unrefereed preprint. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verification, literature research, writing, computation and adversarial review. Those automated reviews are not independent external human peer review; no such human review is claimed.

catalog.title: Integer endpoint discontinuity of normalized uniformization for positively curved surfaces

metadata.title: Integer endpoint discontinuity of normalized uniformization for positively curved surfaces
metadata.description:
For every fixed nonnegative finite integer r, we construct smooth complete metrics of strictly positive Gaussian curvature on both the plane and sphere that converge in ordinary compact-open C^r, while their unique point-normalized uniformizing diffeomorphisms fail compact-open C^(r+1) convergence. The critical r=1 case uses a small C^1 conformal correction controlling the full nonlinear inverse-coordinate curvature operator. This resolves the specified finite-integer endpoint question recorded in the 2017 Oberwolfach report, published on 3 January 2018.

The theorem concerns this specific normalized parametrization of smooth objects and makes no assertion about abstract homeomorphisms, RP^2, smooth or noninteger Holder topologies. Classical logarithmic and twisting mechanisms are credited. A bounded primary-source search through 3 October 2026 did not locate an earlier full geometric resolution, with residual risk of an earlier unindexed realization; exhaustive historical priority is not claimed. The compact support package supplies standalone manuscript source and standard-library exact finite diagnostics. Finite checks supplement the universal proof and do not certify all orders, global curvature, completeness or novelty.

catalog.title: An even-strand Markov calculus for classical and virtual links

metadata.title: An even-strand Markov calculus for classical and virtual links
metadata.description:
We give an explicit elementary affirmative answer to the ordinary-closure interpretation of Problem 42 in the 2014 survey of Fenn, Ilyutko, Kauffman and Manturov. Four reversible algebraic schemes classify ordinary oriented unframed classical link closures using only even-strand braid states. Four additional exchange schemes give the corresponding statement for oriented virtual links. The proof converts the established unrestricted Markov theorems by positively stabilizing every odd-strand vertex and explicitly lifting every generating edge.

Arbitrary finite word blocks and syntactic support bounds are part of the formulation. Minimality, uniform geometric locality, a certificate-search algorithm, historical priority and present openness are not claimed. The note compares its additional schemes with Fiedler's negative conjugation-plus-double-move result without independently certifying his full counterexample proof. It explicitly credits Nencka's related 1996 power-of-two braid announcement; its generalized equivalence and ordinary-closure interpretation are not certified from the two-page source, and historical priority is not asserted. The accompanying compact verification package contains the standalone source, standard-library Python diagnostics, exact results, source qualifications and licenses; finite checks supplement the universal proof. Source-bound literal nonempty left-exchange controls separately verify the index shift and retained buffer. Fuller related Nencka1998/1999 texts have been identified but not accessed, so their bearing on exact ordinary-closure priority remains unresolved.

AI tools were used extensively in construction, drafting, adversarial review and computational verification. This research note is unrefereed; no human peer review or formal proof certification is claimed. The new manuscript and documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0, and the Python code under MIT.

metadata.title: An alternating antimorphic Fine-Wilf theorem
metadata.description: For an arbitrary antimorphic involution theta, a finite word with alternating theta-periods p and q and length at least p+q-gcd(p,q) has alternating theta-period gcd(p,q). This proves the exact unnumbered conjecture after Theorem 23 on printed page 2220 of Nowotka's contribution, joint with Bischoff, to the 2010 Oberwolfach mini-workshop on combinatorics on words. The common finite extension theta(w)w has ordinary periods 2p and 2q; classical Fine-Wilf and central reflection give the alternating conclusion. A reversal example shows that the sufficient formula cannot be reduced by one uniformly; pairwise optimality is not asserted. The research note credits Fine and Wilf, the originating report and Bischoff's thesis, and compares the related Czeizler-Kari-Seki, Kari-Seki and Simpson results. A portable verification supplement preserves the submitted proof, three independent adversarial mathematical audits, complete finite-control outputs and a dated bounded priority audit. No earlier exact theorem was found in the inspected primary sources, without a global novelty or first-discovery certificate; access and version gaps are explicit.
